title: This Bird Hits the Water at 50 mph From 100 Feet Up (and Lives)

scenes.text: This bird hits the water at over 50 miles an hour.
A gannet spots a fish from 100 feet up, folds its wings, and drops like a spear.
That impact would break a human neck. The gannet does it all day.
No outside nostrils, so water can't blast into its skull. Air sacs under the skin act like bubble wrap.
Just before impact, it locks its neck muscles so the spine can't buckle.
Fifty miles an hour. Head first. Again.

description:
Gannets plunge-dive from around 30 metres (100 feet) and hit the water at speeds of more than 50 miles an hour, some reports say close to 60.
They survive because their nostrils open inside the mouth, air sacs under the skin cushion the impact, and a 2016 study found they straighten and brace their neck just before hitting the water so it cannot buckle.
What is the highest thing you have ever jumped off into water? Comment below.
first_comment: Researchers calculated a gannet's neck could in theory survive a dive at nearly 290 kilometres an hour. Which animal would you least want to be for a day?
